chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The thief's hand is cut off for anything that reaches the value of one-fifth of a dinar. And if he stole from crops or fruit or other than that, the way to resolve this is to carry these narrations on the basis of precaution (taqiyyah), because they agree with the views of many of them.

key_terms.يُقْطَعُ: is cut off (referring to the hand)

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum value of goods for hadd al-sariqah (cutting the hand) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-istibsar establishes the nisab for hadd al-sariqah as one-fifth of a dinar, while addressing the apparent contradiction regarding theft from crops by attributing it to taqiyyah to harmonize with other Sunni schools. This reflects the Shia scholarly approach of reconciling specific juristic rulings with broader Islamic consensus through the lens of dissimulation when necessary. The ruling underscores the precision in defining the threshold for corporal punishment in Islamic criminal law.
